lease.policy: The scan has no lease; provider work uses a 5-minute task lease with heartbeat and revision fencing.

idempotency.policy: Minute tick and page task IDs are deterministic; the recipient ledger prevents duplicate delivery.

retry.policy: Durable delivery backs off exponentially from 1 to 60 seconds; each minute scan repairs broken chains.

lease.policy: No route lease; the minute-scoped operation is safe to overlap.

idempotency.policy: The minute tick ID is the required kernel idempotency key; expiry operations also enforce domain guards.

retry.policy: Failures return 503 and the next minute retries against the authoritative current state.

lease.policy: A database-backed delivery ledger claims one pending Slack notification with SKIP LOCKED and a two-minute lease.

idempotency.policy: Error, recovery, and failure deliveries use kind-and-minute keys; hourly heartbeats use a unique ledger key.

retry.policy: Failed Slack deliveries remain pending; every minute drains up to ten, while two overlapping log windows heal one missed schedule.

trigger.reason: Money leaves the provider account, so an operator must review the dry-run and choose the bounded commit size.

slo.objective: Return a dry-run or bounded commit result to the operator within five minutes.

lease.policy: No lease; the operator controls concurrency and the domain recomputes outstanding approval value.

idempotency.policy: Outstanding value is recomputed from the ledger; each transport attempt gets a fresh per-order key.

retry.policy: Dry-run is the default; the operator inspects failures before another commit with limit 3 by default and 50 maximum.

lease.policy: No route lease; bounded candidate work is safe to overlap.

idempotency.policy: Start and trace writes use minute-and-shipment keys; webhook request IDs use the same stable trace key.

retry.policy: The scan is capped at five candidates, delays vendor calls, stops on rate limit, and retries partial failures hourly.

lease.policy: Each task has a 5-minute CAS lease, periodic heartbeat, and revision fence before provider authority.

idempotency.policy: Deterministic task IDs deduplicate enqueue; each provider handler owns its stable delivery key.

retry.policy: Retries back off exponentially from 1 to 60 seconds; each run drains at most 50 claims or 45 seconds.

lease.policy: An account-scoped in-process refresh promise collapses concurrent refreshes within a runtime instance.

idempotency.policy: Persisted expiry is re-read before refresh; a still-usable token bypasses the vendor call.

retry.policy: Accounts fail independently; the next daily schedule retries and request-time token use can refresh earlier.

lease.policy: No route lease; the unbilled-period query and charge guards make overlap safe.

idempotency.policy: Seller-and-period keys, unbilled reads, and deterministic provider order IDs prevent duplicate charges.

retry.policy: Windows and sellers fail independently; each weekly run scans the bounded lookback for missed periods.

lease.policy: Each seller/month has one unique invoice. Point ledger writes and invoice payment commit atomically; provider attempts fence concurrent submissions.

idempotency.policy: The persisted invoice determines the fixed 110,000P funding request key. A pending or unknown PG attempt is never resubmitted. Saved approvals are recovered without another card charge.

retry.policy: Every ten minutes processes at most ten current-month eligible sellers or stale processing invoices. No pre-rollout months are backfilled. Failed bills require operator retry; uncertain funding requires reconciliation.

lease.policy: Due attempts use expiring owner leases; capture transitions lock seller control before attempts and detached uploads claim only their own row.

idempotency.policy: Unique seller/request identities fence starts; confirmed stops detach upload work. Provider 404 or timeout alone never confirms a stop.

retry.policy: Failed phases retain vendor identifiers and next_retry_at; start is never retried after an uncertain response.

trigger.reason: Retains the deployed authenticated retry endpoint for manual recovery; the existing reconcile schedule owns automatic retries.

slo.objective: Process at most 100 due receipts in the selected lane.

lease.policy: Receipt completion and unique ledger keys make overlapping invocations safe.

idempotency.policy: Receipt processed/displayProcessed markers commit with their projections; retries cannot duplicate usage.

retry.policy: Failed receipts retain persistent backoff and are retried by the shared reconcile schedule.

trigger.reason: Retains the deployed authenticated retry endpoint for manual recovery; the existing reconcile schedule owns automatic retries.

slo.objective: Process at most 100 due receipts in the selected lane.

lease.policy: Receipt completion and unique ledger keys make overlapping invocations safe.

idempotency.policy: Receipt processed/displayProcessed markers commit with their projections; retries cannot duplicate usage.

retry.policy: Failed receipts retain persistent backoff and are retried by the shared reconcile schedule.

lease.policy: Receipt completion and seller observation tolerate overlap. Broadcast collection uses a five-minute revision-fenced seller lease and a persisted week cursor. Assessment workers use their own seller advisory transaction locks without blocking receipt writers.

idempotency.policy: Receipt markers commit with projections; observations use seller-and-minute keys. Billing claims key separate durable operations, and canonical payment preparation fences approved or uncertain attempts before any provider call.

retry.policy: Usage and display independently retry at most 100 due receipts with persistent backoff. Billing processes at most two due seller weeks per tick, revisits an eight-week window daily for late usage or declines, and requires reconciliation of uncertain payments. Assessment refresh independently rebuilds up to seven dates per seller, stops starting sellers after 20 seconds, and persists snapshot checkpoints plus retry backoff.

lease.policy: No route lease; seller work and deposit recording are safe to overlap.

idempotency.policy: Each seller uses a minute key and Popbill external deposit IDs are unique in the ledger.

retry.policy: Seller failures are isolated and retried next minute; the three-day query window heals missed schedules.

lease.policy: No route lease; the date-scoped operation is safe to overlap.

idempotency.policy: The KST rate date is the kernel key and ledger uniqueness allows only one published row per day.

retry.policy: The six-hour collection window retries every five minutes and consumers retain the last valid rate.

lease.policy: The session object rejects a second rotation while make-before-break renewal is in flight.

idempotency.policy: Status is re-read before rotation and already-in-flight rotations return a successful skip.

retry.policy: Candidates fail independently and failed status, mint, or rotation work retries in ten minutes.

invariants.description: Cancel coupon balance must equal granted minus consumed plus reversed minus expired plus manual adjustment totals.
Cancel coupon ledger delta must match the semantic direction of grant, consume, reverse, expire, or adjust.
SkuItem.purchasable === (status === 'active' AND stockQty > 0). All reads emitting SkuItem must populate this field; clients consume it as SSOT.
Sku.stockQty and StockLine deltas must keep stockQty >= 0 at every committed state.
Customer block history records only seller-scoped block or unblock actions.
Customer profile status is seller-scoped operational state used by checkout policy, not only a display projection.
Notification messages must always carry a sellerId — every current template belongs to a seller-scoped aggregate.
Order item restocked quantity must never exceed the quantity reserved for fulfillment.
Order payableKrw must equal item subtotal minus item discount plus shipping fees minus point and coupon discounts.
Point balance must equal earned minus spent plus reversed minus expired plus manual adjustment totals.
Point ledger signed amount must match the semantic direction of earn, spend, reverse, expire, or adjust.
User reviews must be anonymous-at-source and seller reviews must carry an explicit display name.
Review hidden/deleted timestamps must agree with the review status.
Settlement batch net amount must equal gross minus refund, processor fee, and platform fee.
Settlement item net amount must equal gross minus refund, processor fee, and platform fee.
A settlement item must carry a stable origin kind/id pair; storage enforces one item per origin.
Settlement source net amount must equal gross minus refund, processor fee, and platform fee.
A settlement source must carry a stable origin kind/id pair; storage enforces uniqueness for that origin.
